name: Hydra - Credential Stuffing
description: Tests known user:password pairs from a single combined file (-C) against a service, rather than every cross product. Use this to replay credentials leaked or found elsewhere against a target (credential stuffing).

examples.label: Try combined user:pass pairs over SSH

notes:
Cred stuffing replays breached user:pass pairs (`-C combo.txt`) against the target - people reuse passwords across services. Low noise vs full brute since each user gets few attempts.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

defense.why_it_works: Reused credentials from breaches work across unrelated services; Hydra replays known user:pass pairs against a login to find reuse.
defense.prerequisites: A list of breached credential pairs and access to the target service.
defense.impact: Access to any account where the user reused a breached password.
defense.detection: Failed authentication bursts: Windows 4625 (failed logon) and 4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failed) at abnormal rate/volume; account lockouts (4740); many attempts from one source, or - for spraying - one password across many accounts. SIEM correlation on failed-logon spikes.
defense.artifacts: Failed and occasional successful logons from breach-sourced pairs; 4625 bursts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux_secure" "Failed password"
| stats count by user, src_ip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where count>10

index=linux sourcetype="linux_secure" "Accepted password"
| stats count by user, src_ip
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "Failed password" or SyslogMessage has "authentication failure"
| extend SrcIP = extract(@"from ([0-9\.]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| summarize attempts=count() by SrcIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where attempts > 10
| sort by attempts desc
// credential stuffing: breach-sourced user:pass pairs, occasional success among many failures
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110 M1032 Multi-factor Authentication] MFA defeats password guessing; [M1027 Password Policies] strong passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on failed-logon spikes and impossible-travel.
defense.evasion: Spray low-and-slow (one password, spaced attempts) to stay under lockout thresholds and volume alerts; distribute across source IPs; target accounts unlikely to be monitored.
defense.misconfiguration: Password policies are insufficiently strict: minimum length too short (< 12 chars), no complexity requirement, no history check (allows password reuse), no lockout or too-lenient lockout threshold. Combined with credential reuse across services, a single cracked hash grants access to multiple systems.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak domain password policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# MinPasswordLength:    8    <-- too short
# PasswordHistoryCount: 0    <-- no history, password reuse allowed
# ComplexityEnabled:    False <-- no complexity
# LockoutThreshold:     0    <-- NO lockout

# Local SAM policy (workgroup machines):
# Control Panel -> Local Security Policy -> Account Policies -> Password Policy
# Same weak defaults as above
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong domain password policy:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -MinPasswordLength 14 \
    -PasswordHistoryCount 24 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true \
    -MaxPasswordAge 90.00:00:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5 \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00

# Fine-Grained PSO for privileged accounts (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name PrivilegedPSO \
    -MinPasswordLength 20 -PasswordHistoryCount 48 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true -LockoutThreshold 3 \
    -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject PrivilegedPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Deploy Azure AD Password Protection (blocks common passwords on-prem too)
# Enable Microsoft Entra ID Smart Lockout

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Linux Audit (auditd), Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Replays known user:password pairs against a service (credential stuffing):
  hydra                    the online cracker
  -C <userpass_list>       a combined file of user:pass pairs - test each pair as-is, not every combination
  ssh://<ip>               the service and target
Use to replay credentials leaked or found elsewhere; the variation shows the http-post-form syntax for web login forms.
